Back-to-School Morning Routine Hacks + How We Built Our Family’s Launch Pad

July 29, 2026 · In: KIDS, LIFE

11 shares

If you’ve been around here for a while, you know mornings and I have a complicated relationship. I am not naturally a morning person (I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again), but with six kids and a school schedule to keep, I’ve learned that a little structure in the morning makes ALL the difference between a day that starts calm and one that starts in chaos.

So as we gear up for another school year, I wanted to come back to two of my favorite topics: building a morning routine that actually works for YOUR family, and creating a “launch pad”, some people call it a command center, we just call it the spot where backpacks stop getting lost, so mornings (and afternoons) run smoother all year long.

Why Mornings Set the Tone for Everything

Here’s the thing I remind myself every single school year: a productive, happy morning leads to a more productive, happy day. That’s true for me, and it’s true for my kids too.

But “productive morning” doesn’t mean the same thing for every family, and it shouldn’t! Some mornings in our house are calm and quiet with a little coffee and cuddles before the chaos begins. Other mornings? Let’s just say there’s a reason I keep a checklist on the fridge.

The goal isn’t perfection, it’s rhythm. Once everyone knows what to expect and where things go, mornings stop feeling like a fire drill.

Start the Routine Before the First Day

One of the biggest mistakes I made in past years was waiting until the first day of school to start our “school morning” routine. Big mistake. Huge.

Now, we start easing into the school-year rhythm about a week or two before the first bell rings:

  • Move bedtime up gradually (about 15 minutes earlier every couple of nights) so the transition doesn’t feel like jet lag. Check out this post on transitioning from Summer to School.
  • Do a “practice morning” or two, going through the motions – getting dressed, eating breakfast, grabbing backpacks – so it’s not brand new on day one. This is especially helpful for the little ones.
  • Use a simple morning checklist (pictures work great for younger kids) so they know the steps without me having to repeat myself fifteen times

Do What You Can the Night Before

This one is non-negotiable in our house. The more we can knock out the night before, the smoother the morning goes:

  • Our kids pick out what they are going to wear and lay their clothes out the night before.
  • Pack backpacks and check for any forms or permission slips.
  • Make lunches (or at least prep what you can) – Check out this blogpost with a free printable with some fun lunch options.
  • Set out breakfast items or portion out anything that needs to be ready to grab.

It sounds simple, but that 10 minutes at night saves 30 minutes of scrambling in the morning.

Building Our Family’s Launch Pad (aka Command Center)

Here’s where the real magic happens, though, not just in the routine, but in the space that supports it.

A launch pad (or command center, or “drop zone” – call it what you want) is simply a designated spot where everything that leaves the house with your kids has a home. Backpacks. Shoes. Lunch boxes. Even the library books that are three days overdue. The launch pad has a place for all of it.

Why Every Family Needs One

If there’s one thing I’ve learned raising six kids, it’s this: if an item doesn’t have an assigned home, it will end up on the floor, in the middle of the walkway, at the worst possible moment on your way out the door.

Creating a launch pad does a few things:

  • It gives kids ownership over their own morning prep (goodbye, “have you seen my other shoe?!”)
  • It cuts down on the morning scavenger hunt for missing items
  • It gives you one central spot to do a quick nightly reset

What Ours Looks Like

Our setup has evolved as our family has grown, but the bones are the same. Our current launch pad is based out of our DIY Mudroom:

  • Hooks at kid-height for backpacks so little ones (and big ones) can hang their own bag without help
  • A basket or bin per kid (or per category – shoes, library books, etc.) so everything has an obvious spot
  • A rolling cart for homework and school supplies that can tuck out of the way when it’s not in use – this has been one of our best additions over the years.
  • A designated shelf in the pantry for lunchbox supplies, so packing lunches doesn’t turn into a kitchen-wide search

The key is putting it somewhere your family will actually use – for us, that’s near the door we leave from most often, not some far corner of the house that looks nice but gets ignored.

Make It a Team Effort

Whatever your launch pad looks like, get your kids involved in setting it up. When they help choose the bins or decide where their hooks go, they’re a lot more likely to actually use it (and a lot less likely to leave their backpack in the middle of the hallway, well, that’s the goal).

A Simple Truth About Mornings

At the end of the day, the goal isn’t a Pinterest-perfect entryway or a rigid, no-room-for-error schedule. It’s giving your family a rhythm and a space that makes the mornings just a little easier, so you can actually enjoy those last few minutes of cuddles before the day gets going.

What does your family’s morning routine or launch pad look like? I’d love to hear your best tips in the comments!
